findings.title: diffPaired replaces whole array items, so unchanged members appear in the patch
findings.why: When two array items are paired as changed in place, `diffPaired` compares the stringified length of the nested ops with that of a whole-item `replace`. It emits the `replace` when the nested ops are not shorter. The spec says unchanged members MUST NOT appear in any path or value, and that a change must be expressed at the deepest differing location. Example: `createPatch([{k:1,x:2}], [{k:1,y:3}])`. The nested ops are `remove /0/x` plus `add /0/y`, which is longer than `replace /0` with `{k:1,y:3}`. The patch therefore replaces the whole item and mentions the unchanged `k`. Large unchanged siblings, or a change next to a long path, behave the same way. Round-trip tests still pass, so nothing catches this. I checked this by reading the code and did not run it.
